chunks.text: لَبَّیْكَ اَللّٰهُمَّ لَبَّیْكَ، لَبَّیْكَ لَا شَرِیْكَ لَكَ لَبَّیْكَ، اِنَّ الْحَمْدَ، وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَاشَرِیْكَ لَكَ۔ لَبَّیْكَ اَللّٰهُمَّ لَبَّیْكَ، لَبَّیْكَ لَا شَرِیْكَ لَكَ لَبَّیْكَ، اِنَّ الْحَمْدَ، وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَاشَرِیْكَ لَكَ۔

لَبَّیْكَ اَللّٰهُمَّ لَبَّیْكَ، لَبَّیْكَ لَا شَرِیْكَ لَكَ لَبَّیْكَ، اِنَّ الْحَمْدَ، وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَاشَرِیْكَ لَكَ۔ اَللّٰهُمَّ لَبَّیْكَ، لَبَّیْكَ لَا شَرِیْكَ لَكَ لَبَّیْكَ، اِنَّ الْحَمْدَ، وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَاشَرِیْكَ لَكَ۔ اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ. اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ.

Assalamu alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh everyone. We welcome you to a very beautiful course because it is about Hajj. Hajj is beautiful, that's why this course Insha'Allah we're gonna hope that it is going to turn beautiful for all of us. May Allah enable us to go for Hajj over and over again, Ameen. So Alhamdulillah, really good to see all of you here. So is everyone ready to begin? Alhamdulillah. Is there anyone going for Hajj this year? Or planning to go for Hajj this year? Making du'as to go for Hajj this year?

اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ. May Allah enable all of us to go there over and over again, Ameen. So if not this year, Insha'Allah next year, right? Don't worry. So make a plan, start saving up for it, and Insha'Allah don't just rely on your own means, rely on Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala; He can take you there.

SubhanAllah. All right, so let's begin properly. اِنَّ الْحَمْدَ لِلّٰهِ، نَحْمَدُهٗ وَنَسْتَعِیْنُهٗ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهٗ، وَنَعُوْذُ بِاللّٰهِ مِنْ شُرُوْرِ اَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَیِّئٰتِ اَعْمَالِنَا، مَنْ یَّهْدِهِ اللّٰهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهٗ، وَمَنْ یُّضْلِلْهُ فَلَا هَادِیَ لَهٗ، وَاَشْهَدُ اَنْ لَّاۤ اِلٰهَ اِلَّا اللّٰهُ وَحْدَهٗ لَا شَرِیْكَ لَهٗ،

وَاَشْهَدُ اَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهٗ وَرَسُوْلُهٗ۔ اَعُوْذُ بِاللّٰهِ مِنَ الشَّیْطٰنِ الرَّجِیْمِ۔ بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِیْمِ۔ رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِیْ صَدْرِیْ ۙ وَیَسِّرْ لِیْۤ اَمْرِیْ ۙ وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّنْ لِّسَانِیْ ۙ یَفْقَهُوْا قَوْلِیْ۔ اَللّٰهُمَّ فَقِّهْنَا فِی الدِّیْنِ. May Allah give us the correct understanding of our deen, Ameen. So with that,

Insha'Allah let's begin our session. Today's session will be more like an orientation day. The name of the course is 'Hajj: Journey of a Lifetime' because it is, SubhanAllah, a very beautiful journey, and it is a journey of a lifetime for some, and Alhamdulillah some people are able to go over and over again. May Allah accept everyone's efforts and may Allah accept everyone's wishes and desires to go for Hajj as well, Ameen. Because not everyone is able to go, but Alhamdulillah we all, being believers, we wish to go there, right? But SubhanAllah,

someone was mentioning something very powerful: that there are three types of people when it comes to Hajj. There are three types of people when it comes to Hajj: one type, they can afford and they also want to go; second type, they cannot afford, but they still want to go; third type, they can afford, but they don't go, they delay it, they don't really, really want to go, SubhanAllah. So may Allah save us from becoming from the third category, Ameen. So Alhamdulillah for this opportunity that we are able to go, and Alhamdulillah after two years Hajj has opened up—not fully, but Alhamdulillah it has opened up for many people, Alhamdulillah. So you can say slightly a door has opened. Alhamdulillah there is hope that Insha'Allah in coming years it's going to be back to normal or even Insha'Allah better for everyone. So Alhamdulillah when we have got this opportunity, when we know that Hajj is open, that Insha'Allah we should increase in our du'as so that we can actually get there.

And whenever Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala gives us the opportunity, we should just avail it right away before it's too late. So let's begin by praising Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala that we are still alive. Let's praise Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala that we are Muslims. Let's praise Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala that Alhamdulillah He enabled us to join this session, because Insha'Allah when we learn about Hajj, the goal is that we love Hajj more, and when we are going to yearn for Hajj more, Insha'Allah the du'as are going to come from our hearts, right?

All right, so let's praise Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala: اَللّٰهُمَّ لَكَ الْحَمْدُ حَتّٰی تَرْضٰی، وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ اِذَا رَضِیْتَ، وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ بَعْدَ الرِّضٰی. O Allah, for You is praise until You're pleased with our praise, and for You is praise when You are pleased, and for You is praise after You're pleased. اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ كَثِیْرًا.

اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ عَدَدَ مَا خَلَقَ. And Alhamdulillah we are going to begin with this beautiful du'a because this is such a beautiful du'a and very powerful du'a which talks about four important things. We're asking Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala for four things in this du'a: بَرَكَات (barakat), رَحْمَة (rahmat), فَضْل (fadl), and رِزْق (rizq). اَللّٰهُمَّ ابْسُطْ عَلَيْنَا مِنْ بَرَكَاتِكَ، وَرَحْمَتِكَ، وَفَضْلِكَ، وَرِزْقِكَ. O Allah, give us in abundance—what?

From Your blessings, Your mercy, Your favors, and Your sustenance. Ameen. May Allah accept this du'a for all of us. Isn't it a beautiful du'a? It covers pretty much everything, SubhanAllah. So Insha'Allah with this we are going to Insha'Allah hope that Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala blesses us and also blesses us in our knowledge about Hajj, Ameen. So the question is: why do you want to learn about Hajj? Like why this year? Why in 2022? Why do you want to learn about Hajj?

Very good, Sister Afreen. Sister Afreen is saying to perform the Hajj persona—beautiful. Anything else? Why do you want to learn about Hajj? So it becomes accepted. May Allah accept it from all the people who actually go and perform it, Ameen. To learn the right way so Allah accepts her Hajj—very good, Alhamdulillah. Any other reason? For Hajj Mabroor, yes. To perform it like the Prophet Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam. For the acceptance. To know the importance in the right way—perfect.

Alhamdulillah. To know the wisdom behind this ibadah, so we can follow the way of Rasulullah Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam, so our effort and time is not wasted. Beautiful, well done. Masha'Allah, all of you have really good ideas about why to go for Hajj. No one said that we want to be called Hajis; no one said that because, you know, everyone in my family they've already been there, it was only me who was left. Alhamdulillah, that's good. So it seems like Alhamdulillah we are on the right page. Insha'Allah we're going to kind of tweak our intention a bit more Insha'Allah.

So what's the benefit of going for Umrah or Hajj? Rasulullah Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam said: The performance of Umrah is an expiation for the sins committed between one Umrah and the next, right? And the reward of Hajj Mabroor is nothing except Jannah, SubhanAllah. Like it's like guaranteed, and Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala's promises are true. So to fulfill the most important journey of one's life with sincerity for the sake of Allah, this should be our goal:

to fulfill the most important journey of one's life. You may travel here and there, but this is going to be Insha'Allah the best journey of your life, most important journey of your life. So how are we supposed to take this journey? With sincerity, with ikhlas. Why? For the sake of Allah, only for the sake of Allah. Not for fame, not for name, not for some games, not for some business. We should Insha'Allah keep it as pure as possible. Why? Because Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala commanded us to do that:

وَاَتِمُّوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ لِلّٰهِ ؕ 'And complete the Hajj and 'Umrah for Allah.' Like it doesn't say complete the Hajj and Umrah and it doesn't stop there, it says لِلّٰهِ: do it for Allah, don't do it for any other reason. So Insha'Allah our goal is that we will Insha'Allah perform Hajj and Umrah whenever we get a chance only for the pleasure of Allah, not the pleasure of people. Only for the pleasure of Allah, only we want Allah to be happy with us, only we want the approval of Allah, we don't want the approval of people.

So in order to do this, we need to ask ourselves a few questions, and one of them is: why am I going for Hajj? Like why? Why am I saving up for Hajj? Why do I yearn to go for Hajj? What is the intention? And Insha'Allah we have to be truthful to ourselves in order to fix our intention. If it's any other reason—and it sometimes is—then Insha'Allah this is the time to fix it before it's too late, before we perform it, right? So Insha'Allah if you did not do your Hajj yet, and if you're going this year, then Insha'Allah this is the time to fix your intention.

And we've got to Insha'Allah make it a habit that we actually ask ourselves before doing other actions as well that: why am I praying? Why am I fasting? Why am I giving sadaqah? All of these questions are going to help us keep our intentions purely for Allah, and this is a way to keep a check on our intentions. So Insha'Allah just make it a habit: keep asking and keep giving yourself honest answers. Honest answers will help you Insha'Allah fix the intention issues,

because intention is something which is very risky; it keeps changing because shaytan is there, our nafs is there, right? And our influences are there, our company sometimes, you know, they make us think something which is not correct. So Insha'Allah in order to keep ourselves away from all of this, and above and beyond from petty reasons and petty purposes, we need to keep asking ourselves these questions so that we can fix our intention before it gets too late. And why the intention is so

important, this Hadith gives us a very good idea about it: A man came to Rasulullah and said: 'What do you think of a man who fights seeking reward and fame, what will he have?' Rasulullah said: 'He will not have anything.' SubhanAllah, think about it: this person is putting his life at stake, yet he's not going to get anything out of it because he had a double intention. So when people are going for Hajj, they need to remind themselves that it should only be for Allah, it should only be to please Allah, it should not be to please people, it should not be for any other reason, it should not be for fame. So may Allah protect us from all wrong intentions. So Insha'Allah in this course we will learn about different steps of Hajj, how to perform them, and also what are the rewards of each step, SubhanAllah.

So that is going to help us when we perform Hajj to enjoy Hajj, because a lot of times people take it as a burden, people take it as a chore or just a to-do list item on their list when they're doing Hajj. But we want to do better, Insha'Allah. We don't want to do, you know, all the rituals of Hajj, all the rites of Hajj, just as chores; we actually want to enjoy each and every step, and we will enjoy once we have knowledge about it, Insha'Allah. So we will know about every step of Hajj, and we will try to perform it according to the Sunnah, Insha'Allah. We'll also learn about the do's and don'ts of Hajj, and then Insha'Allah we will prepare for Hajj before we go there. Even if you're not going this year, we can still start preparing for it, because the more we are prepared, the better it is for us; the more we know, the more we will be able to, Insha'Allah,

have confidence when we're performing our Hajj. And people won't be able to confuse us, because a lot of times when you end up there with no knowledge or little knowledge, a lot of people are there to confuse you because there are so many opinions, there's so many people, there's so many different backgrounds, and they just share whatever they have heard. A lot of times they also don't have knowledge, and then they baffle you easily when you don't know enough. So Insha'Allah in this course you're going to know, so that we are not baffled, Insha'Allah. And it is the promise of Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala that He will give us Jannah for Hajj Mabroor, and Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala's promises are true. So Insha'Allah keep this in mind when you're going, and Insha'Allah you will come back sin-free as a newborn.

You will be just like a newborn baby with no sins on your record, SubhanAllah. So that is our biggest motivation when we go for Hajj, Alhamdulillah. Hajj is an important part of our deen, so we should prepare for it spiritually and heartily, wholeheartedly Insha'Allah, right? So we should prepare our body, we should prepare our finances, we should prepare our soul, we should prepare our intellect, we should prepare our heart, and Insha'Allah go well prepared for Hajj, Insha'Allah. So now we are going to look at some of the tips given by Sister Shazia Nawaz: that how to prepare for Hajj. So there are eleven in total. So I hope you have received your workbook from your course portal. So Insha'Allah download the workbook and Insha'Allah start jotting down all the points. If you don't have the workbook because you're not part of the course, it's okay, you can write down on a piece of paper.

All right, ready everyone? How many points were there again? Eleven in total. So let's just begin. Beautiful! First one: make du'a for ikhlas, right? We have talked about that we should keep a check on our intention: it should be sincere, it should be khalis. Now we need to make du'a for it as well, because our efforts are not enough; our efforts cannot take us anywhere. We always need Allah's help. So Insha'Allah first thing, ask Allah for help: make du'a for ikhlas. There are so many du'as for ikhlas; Insha'Allah we're going to cover another one tomorrow, but today we're going to look at this beautiful one, because this talks about our goal as well as we have learned about it earlier: only for Allah, right? So our goal is that we want to see Allah. So what is this beautiful du'a?

اَللّٰهُمَّ اَسْئَلُكَ لَذَّةَ النَّظَرِ اِلٰی وَجْهِكَ، وَالشَّوْقَ اِلٰی لِقَائِكَ فِیْ غَيْرِ ضَرَّاءَ مُضِرَّةٍ وَّلَا فِتْنَةٍ مُّضِلَّةٍ۔ What does that mean? 'O Allah, indeed I ask You for the sweetness of looking upon Your Face and a longing to meet You, in a manner that does not entail a calamity that will bring about harm or a trial that will cause deviation.'

Insha'Allah Sister Shazia Nawaz is going to explain this du'a to us towards the end of the session, Insha'Allah. So if you have any questions, you can keep those questions till the end. Point number two: in order to prepare for Hajj, we should start observing our fara'id—mandatory prayers—and nawafil properly. So not just observe them, but also observe them on time, follow all the prerequisites, and do everything properly. Start off with

proper wudu, Insha'Allah, and get in the mode of prayers. And SubhanAllah a lot of us, we do pray, but Insha'Allah now we need to move it up a notch, we need to make it better. Especially when we are going for Hajj, we are going to a very beautiful place, we are going to visit sacred masajid: we will be in Makkah, we will be in Madinah, Masjid al-Haram, Masjid an-Nabawi. So Insha'Allah we should try our best to pray beautifully and on time. A lot of times it has been seen that people, they actually reach there, but whatever happens, sometimes they get sick or sometimes, you know, they don't have enough motivation to go to the masjid to pray. That's something which is very sad, because we know about the rewards, right? The reward of praying in Masjid al-Haram is like praying 100,000 prayers elsewhere,

and the reward of praying in Masjid an-Nabawi is like praying 1,000 prayers elsewhere, SubhanAllah. The reward is that massive, so we should not just take it lightly and not go to the masjid and thinking, 'We are still in the sacred bounds in our hotel room, so we'll still pray here.' If there's a genuine problem, that's a different story. But if you're able to walk, if you're able to, you know, go down to the masjid, please do that; don't be lazy about it.

And Insha'Allah for that we should start making du'as right away: that may Allah grant us the ability to pray all five prayers in the sacred masajid when we are there, whenever we are there, all five prayers in the masajid. Because what's the point of going there and still not getting all that reward which we can easily avail, Insha'Allah? So make a plan for it and make du'as for it. And another tip which will help you is that Insha'Allah when you are going to be there, whenever Insha'Allah, let's make du'a that we get there soon. So if you're not going for Hajj this year, you can Insha'Allah plan for an Umrah trip, all right Insha'Allah. So whenever you get there, then Insha'Allah this is our goal: that we're going to pray all five prayers in the masjid. So the tip is that when you're going to go to the masjid from your hotel room, you're going to wear your abaya and hijab, isn't it?

Or if you're brothers, you're gonna dress up accordingly. So how about, if you're going for Hajj and Umrah, before you go there, like if you're going for Hajj this year, this is the time to Insha'Allah start preparing for it: so wear your abaya and hijab before salah anyways so that you get in the mode of it, so that you know that: okay, I'll have to do it five times a day when I'm there, or even more, because sometimes you'll just go for tawaf, sometimes you will just go for tahajjud, sometimes you will just go for prayers, just like that Insha'Allah. So get in that mode, that before you pray, you actually prepare yourself.

So this way when you reach there, it won't be some extra task for you; you will already be kind of in routine for that. And point number three is: get in the habit of reciting the Qur'an after every prayer. Why after every prayer? Because Insha'Allah in masajid there you will have a lot of time: you won't have to worry about cooking food, you won't have to worry about serving anyone, you won't have to worry about work. So Alhamdulillah all the time you will have is for worship, so what is better than reciting the Qur'an, right? Alhamdulillah. So when you are done with your tawaf, when you're done with your nawafil, what are you going to do? Instead of sitting and chitchatting, Insha'Allah open your Mushaf and start praying. It's a good idea to have your own Mushaf Insha'Allah, even though in both masajid or in any masjid you go there, you will find Insha'Allah a lot of Mushafs there; you can find the copies of the Qur'an there, you can easily grab them and recite. But if you have your own, then Insha'Allah you won't have to run around looking for them,

and you won't have to find the place where you stopped before, because you will have some type of bookmark Insha'Allah. So all of this will help you. So why recite a lot of Qur'an? Because Insha'Allah for every letter you're getting ten rewards, and there's so many other benefits—you know all about them. If you are memorizing the Qur'an, then Alhamdulillah that's another beautiful opportunity for you there, that you can just start reviewing it, and then Insha'Allah whatever you review you can Insha'Allah recite that in your salah in order to strengthen your memorization. Point

number four: give sadaqah. Try to give daily sadaqah while you're there. So take some extra money with you, and then Insha'Allah try to give as much sadaqah as possible to different people, and Insha'Allah may Allah accept all of it from you. And when you're giving daily sadaqah, don't just forget about other forms of sadaqah. So give money as well for sure, for sure, even if it's not a lot; but give every time you come across someone you think you should give to that person.

Otherwise you can buy meals and give people meals. A lot of people are waiting there hungry and it's very hard for them to go and grab food. So if you notice someone who's hungry sitting outside the masjid and is not even able to go inside for whatever reason—sometimes there are some restrictions, children sometimes are not allowed to go to the masjid so the mothers they have to wait outside with the kids—so Insha'Allah if you have some snacks you can share with them.

You can give them energy bars, you can give them food packs, whatever you can, Insha'Allah, that's a very good opportunity while you are going to get a lot of other rewards for your other types of acts of worship might as well for sadaqah Insha'Allah, and other forms of sadaqah would include giving Hajj gifts. So Insha'Allah your Hajj gift can include method: how to perform Hajj. Because sadly it has been seen many people—not few, many people—when they reach there, they don't know what to do and they're just relying on their groups,

they're relying on their agents, they're relying on their group leads, they're relying on their scholars. It's good that you have a group lead, it's good that you have a good group you're with, but you also need to know what to do, because sometimes people actually do get lost there from their group, and then they're very lost because they were just relying on their leads; if leads are not there, then they are lost. So it's good that we know. But let's say the people around us, if they don't know, we can give them small pamphlets of authentic

ones: how to perform Hajj and whatnot. That would be a very beneficial gift. Also the du'a books are a very good idea; make sure they're authentic du'as. So Insha'Allah whatever you share, it should be authentic. So sometimes it's not allowed for us to share literature inside the masjid, but it's okay to share outside the masjid or it's okay to share with the people you know. So the people who are with you in your group, or the people who are from your country, or the people you're friends with, or new friends you make at the masjid. So Insha'Allah you can

share such information with them, such gifts with them. And other things you can also give them, not just the books, but Insha'Allah anything else you buy from there you can give it to them; you can buy from your homeland or wherever you're living and you can take the stuff with you and you give them as gifts. Also you will see that even though Zamzam water is right there, but you know some people are so old and you know sometimes it's very tiring to go to the cooler, get the water. So what you can do is whenever you go drink Zamzam water, you can just take some extra and then extra back to your row or anywhere you see some elderly ladies or elderly men, if you're a brother, then you can Insha'Allah share that water with them, and that will be Insha'Allah another act of charity on your behalf. Very interesting question: do they give you food there? Yes, if you go with Hajj groups they arrange food for you, otherwise there are so many restaurants, people can order their own food as well whatever they like, and Allah knows best.

And then point number five: ask for forgiveness often in the morning and evening. Why? Because istighfar makes things easy, isn't it? So Insha'Allah don't ever forget to ask for forgiveness. Don't ever think that: 'I'm here because I'm so noble and so holy; rest of the family members they never got a chance or they didn't get a chance this year, so I'm better.' Never ever, right? So don't ever become arrogant and always stay humble and keep asking Allah for forgiveness, that you know, with all our faults, with all our shortcomings, still Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala invited us, so O Allah forgive us, because we can make mistakes there as well,

so we need to keep asking Allah for forgiveness. When you're asking for forgiveness, when you're saying, then Astaghfirullah, or Allahummaghfirli, or Rabbighfirli, think about your shortcomings, think about your faults, think about your sins, and then remember the blessings and the benefits of istighfar when you're doing that. And remember Rasulullah, he also would ask Allah to forgive him 70 to 100 times a day, SubhanAllah.

So where do we stand when we try to compare ourselves with this amazing action of our Prophet? So 'Astaghfirullah' is the easiest way to ask Allah for forgiveness, but Alhamdulillah there are many beautiful adhkar, many beautiful du'as to ask Allah for forgiveness. So Insha'Allah if you know more that's even better. Safe from all evils, SubhanAllah, because Makkah is a cradle of peace and security,

peace and security, and you feel it, SubhanAllah. And Ibrahim actually made this du'a: وَاِذْ قَالَ اِبْرٰهٖمُ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هٰذَا بَلَدًا اٰمِنًا. When Ibrahim said, 'My Lord, make this city secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols,' his concern was that we don't do shirk; he wanted safety not for worldly reasons, he wanted safety for worship reasons, and Allah knows best. And we also learn about two other qualities of Baytullah from Surah Al-Baqarah, that it is called مَثَابَةً and أَمْنًا. Masaba is a place where people return, and that's why, SubhanAllah, people keep returning.

Anytime we go there, we just want to come back again. It's very hard to leave those sacred lands, it's very hard to leave Kaaba; people who go there, they want to keep going back, SubhanAllah. Masaba: a place of return, SubhanAllah.

And Amna is security. How is Makkah a place of safety and security? We're going to cover six points, but I really want all of you to jot down only the four points first—the first four points only at this point, because we are going to touch the other points if you get a chance in this course. First point: sacred place till Qiyamah. Makkah is going to stay sacred till Qiyamah; we need to remember that it's a sanctuary till the Day of Resurrection. Rasulullah, he said that on the day of conquest of Makkah:

'There is no migration now, there is no hijra now, but there is jihad and good intentions. And when you are called for jihad, you should come out at once.' Rasulullah also said on the day of conquest of Makkah: 'Allah has made this town, this Makkah, a sanctuary since the day He created the heavens and the earth. So, it is a sanctuary by Allah's decree till the Day of Resurrection,' SubhanAllah. So, since beginning till end, it is a sacred and safe place; it is a safe zone not only for people, but also for animals and plants. And you're going to love this hadith, Insha'Allah:

Narrated Ibn Abbas: 'On the day of the conquest of Makkah, Rasulullah said: Allah has made this town a sanctuary; its thorny bushes should not be cut, its game should not be chased'—like you're not supposed to hunt there—'and its fallen things should not be picked up except by the one who would announce it publicly,' right? So, if you see anything dropped, you're not supposed to pick it up unless you're able to get this back to the owner or you know how to get it to the authorities so that they can get that item back to the person who owns it or who dropped it. And then third point: anyone leaving for the House of Allah is in Allah's protection. That's another beautiful point, SubhanAllah. So, we learn from a narration: 'Three are under Allah's guarantee:

a man who goes to the masjid from the masajid of Allah, and the soldier who leaves in the way of Allah, and a person who leaves for Hajj.' When we leave for Hajj, we are under Allah's guarantee, like He is going to take care of us, SubhanAllah.

First, SubhanAllah. And then fourth point: safety from Dajjal's fitna. We all are scared about Dajjal, isn't it? So, SubhanAllah Makkah is safe from Dajjal, Masjid al-Haram is safe from Dajjal. So, let's look at the narration now: Rasulullah said: 'There will be no town which Dajjal will not enter except Makkah and Medina, and there will be no entrance road of both Makkah and Medina but the angels will be standing in rows guarding it against him.' And then Medina will shake with its inhabitants thrice, earthquakes will come, and Allah will expel all the disbelievers and the Munafiqeen from it. So, only the pure people will stay in Medina, SubhanAllah.

So, they will not run away and they will stay safe from Dajjal. So, let's move on to the next part of this ayah where we learned that we are supposed to do Hajj for Allah. Again, SubhanAllah, even that is something we have learned before from Surah Al-Baqarah, we learn the same thing: وَلِلّٰهِ عَلَی النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَیْتِ. For Allah, what are we supposed to do?

People are obliged to do Hajj for Allah, not for any other reason, not for business, not for money, not for fame, nothing else, just for Allah. مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ اِلَیْهِ سَبِیْلًا—whoever is able to do it. We are going to talk about the ability, we are going to talk about what is istita'ah in a bit.

But before that, let's just revisit the goal: that why do we do Hajj? We do Hajj only for the pleasure of Allah, only to get His approval, only to please Him, only to obey Him, only to respond to His call. May Allah make us among those people who do that! And Hajj is mandatory once in a lifetime, but if we perform more Hajj it's better for us. And Insha'Allah we are going to touch base that point today if time permits, Insha'Allah.

So, what's the proof that Hajj is mandatory for those who are able to go? He was given khutbah and he said: 'O people, Allah has made Hajj an obligation for you, so perform Hajj.' Thereupon a person said, 'Is it to be performed every year?' Rasulullah Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam, he kept quiet, but this person repeated his question three times.

Whereupon Allah's Messenger said: 'If I were to say yes, it would become obligatory and you would not be able to do it.' Then he said: 'Leave me with what I have left to you, for those who were before you were destroyed because of excessive questioning.' So, Allah He just clarified that it is mandatory only once. So, that's the proof for that.

And there's another narration which we have already covered before, and I'm going to show you that today as well. So, Hajj is mandatory for those who are able to go, who have istita'ah. What does that mean? It has three understandings based: first one, when a person has the travel expenses, when a person is able to travel, then he is capable to go for Hajj. And also this person should have enough expenses for the people he's leaving behind.

So, let's say if he is the father of the family and he has family left behind, so he should leave enough funds for them to eat, drink, and survive. So, this means this person is rich enough to go for Hajj, because that person has money to go for Hajj and also his family is not going to suffer. Second point: that it should be safe, it should be safe to go.

So, scholars have mentioned in the tafaseer: safe way, when a person's life and property is safe, then it's okay for us to go. But if it's not safe, then it's not mandatory for us to go that year if there's a problem. So, Alhamdulillah because of this opinion, the COVID years were okay for us if we were not able to go, because it wasn't safe for our life, isn't it, SubhanAllah? And if people were not called for Hajj or they were not allowed to go for Hajj or Umrah, then it wasn't something so bad, it's totally allowed based on all of these narrations. And then if a person is not physically able to go, then again that person is not required to go. So, physical capability is also one of the conditions.

So, let's say a person is not able to go, but is rich enough—can that person send someone else on his or her behalf with her money or with his money? Yes, right? And Allah knows best. So, the people who don't perform Hajj in spite of the ability to go for Hajj—you know, they have money, they are healthy enough, and there is no problem on the way—then it is considered a major sin. Not performing Hajj in spite of one's ability is a major sin.

But there is something to remember: this person believes that Hajj is fard, but not going because of laziness, because of whatever. But believing that Hajj is not mandatory or Hajj is not part of Islam makes a person a non-believer, kicks a person out of the fold of Islam. So, it's something which is very important to remember.

So, two things, Insha'Allah, we need to remember, because the next part of the ayah—which is the concluding part of the ayah we have covered: وَمَنْ كَفَرَ—whoever disbelieves... The beginning part talks about Hajj, it would have mentioned, you know, the one who doesn't do Hajj; but here it is mentioned the one who does kufr. What does that mean? It's the kufr of the blessing: Allah has given you health, Allah has given you wealth, Allah has made it easy for you to reach there, and you still are not going.

You are denying the blessing, and this blessing can be denied with heart and with actions. When this blessing is denied with heart, then the person doesn't believe in Hajj. When this blessing is denied with action, then person doesn't go for Hajj, believes in it but doesn't do it. So, both are wrong. So, whoever doesn't go for Hajj, then they need to remember: فَاِنَّ اللّٰهَ غَنِیٌّ عَنِ الْعٰلَمِیْنَ— Allah is Ghani, He doesn't need your Hajj, He doesn't need you. So, we don't do any favor on anyone when we do Hajj, it's a favor on us.

Now, let's just do some definitions. We have covered them yesterday as well briefly, but Insha'Allah today we're going to touch base those same definitions, so please jot them down if you can. So, the definition of Hajj or the meaning of Hajj linguistically is: to intend to go to a respectable thing again and again.

Hajj is the masdar of Hajj, and this is what it means: to intend to go to a respectable thing again and again. And in Sharia, in terminology, the definition of Hajj is: the act of performing the prescribed acts of worship by attending certain places on the days prescribed by the Sharia. Insha'Allah we're going to learn about the days, we're going to learn about the places, and we also are going to learn about the acts; but for now, just know the definition: the act of performing the prescribed acts of worship by attending certain places, by visiting certain places on the days prescribed by the Sharia.

And the one who performs Hajj is called 'Hajj' in Arabic. In Urdu, in other languages, you must have heard the term 'Hajji', right? But it's Hajj in Arabic. Hajj is fine too, depends which language you're using to speak. And what's the plural of Hajj? There are two plurals: one is Hujjaj and one is Hajeej, both mean the ones who are performing Hajj.

And Hajj was obligated in 9th Hijri, and Abu Bakr, he was sent as the lead for the first Hajj group after it became mandatory, right? So, Hajj was obligated in 9th Hijri, and Muslims did perform Hajj that year, and Abu Bakr, he was leading them, SubhanAllah. Rasulullah, he did not go this

year, and we're going to learn about the reason in a bit. And when Muslims reached there and they performed Hajj, it was announced in the 9th Hijri that no one will perform Hajj naked after this day, no one will perform Hajj without clothes because this is what Mushrikeen would do, and no Mushrikeen will perform Hajj next year after this. And Rasulullah, he performed his first and last Hajj in 10th Hijri, and it was a shirk-free Hajj. Why? Because there were no idols there anymore near Kaaba—if you remember the history, Mushrikeen had placed a lot of idols around Kaaba,

so they were removed. And also Mushrikeen were not allowed to come for Hajj this year. So, it was a shirk-free Hajj, and no sinful actions were involved in this Hajj. Rasulullah taught people Hajj with his actions and his words, and we call this Hajj 'Hajjat al-Wada' —the farewell Hajj, the only Hajj, Hajjat al-Wada'. And you must have heard about the khutbah which is very famous—the sermon of Hajjat al-Wada'—which is quoted over and over again because it has beautiful teachings for all of us, Insha'Allah if time permits we can also go over it.

Let's just talk about a few things we have already covered yesterday. I'm just going to quickly go over them, just jot down the title parts, right? Just know the main headings, Insha'Allah. Hajj is an obligation, and it's a very important obligation, it's a command of Allah, and also Rasulullah Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam, he emphasized it. And if a person wants to perform more Hajj, they can, and Insha'Allah we will cover that narration in a bit as well. And don't delay Hajj if Allah has given you enough, and if you fulfill all three conditions of istita'ah, then Insha'Allah go and don't delay it for petty reasons or for worldly reasons. And once Hajj becomes an obligation, do it before anything else.

And Hajj does not get waived—this is something we haven't discussed yesterday, so let's talk about that. A man said, 'My father has died, and he did not perform Hajj; shall I perform Hajj on his behalf?' Rasulullah Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam said: 'Don't you think that if your father owed a debt, you would pay off?' The man said, 'Yes.' He said, 'That debt owed to Allah is more deserving of being paid off,' SubhanAllah, right? So, if a person dies, his salah is not supposed to be prayed by anyone, but his Hajj or her Hajj is supposed to be performed by the heirs, just like fasting is, right? Fasting doesn't just get waived for the previous years; if a person has missed some fast, these fasts are to be made up by the heirs, by the family. So, Insha'Allah something to remember. So, it's better that we perform our mandatory Hajj before we die so that it doesn't become a burden for the people after us.

And Hajj is a very important pillar of our deen. Let's talk about the importance of Hajj. First of all, why is it important? Because it's a command of Allah, that's why it's important. It is called the rope of Islam, strong bond of Islam—that's why it's important. Let's look at this beautiful narration about rope of Islam or strong bond of Islam: Sahaba mentioned that we were sitting with Rasulullah, so one of them mentioned that we were sitting with Rasulullah and he asked: 'Which bond of Islam is the strongest?' Sahaba said, 'The salah.' He said, 'Good.' 'And what next?' They said, 'Zakah.' He said, 'Good.' 'And what next?'

They said, 'Fast of Ramadan.' He said, 'Good.' 'And what next?' And they said, 'Hajj.' He said, 'Good.' And this narration goes on, but SubhanAllah it shows the basic pillars of Islam right here. And Hajj and Umrah, they are the identity of a Muslim. No one else goes for Hajj and Umrah, right, that you won't be confused if someone tells you that, 'I went for Hajj,' you won't be like, 'Maybe this person is a Muslim or not?' You won't be, because only Muslims do that,

SubhanAllah. Even Umar narrates from his father Umar and from Rasulullah about the question of Jibreel which he asked about Islam, so Rasulullah responded to that question with this answer: 'Islam is that you bear witness that there is no god except Allah and Muhammad is the messenger of Allah Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam, and that you establish prayer, you pay zakah, you perform Hajj, you perform Umrah, and perform ghusl of janabah, and perform complete wudu, and fast in Ramadan.' Jibreel asked, 'Do I become a Muslim when I do that?'

Rasulullah said, 'Yes,' SubhanAllah. So, all of these are the signs of a believer, all of these are the things Muslims do. And Hajj is exclusively for Muslims, especially after the Hajj of 9th Hijri, so starting from 10th Hijri only Muslims performed Hajj, SubhanAllah. And Sahaba would include Hajj in major good deeds.

Let's look at this narration about Abu Huraira: he quoted Rasulullah saying: 'When the Muslim slave performs the due of Allah and the due of his master, he will have two rewards,' right? So, double reward for a Muslim who is not free. Abu Huraira said: 'By the One in Whose hand my soul is in, if jihad for the sake of Allah, Hajj, and kindness to my mother had not come in the way, I would have liked death to come to me while I was a slave.'

Why? Because he wanted double ajr. But because he knew that Hajj and kindness to the mother and striving in the way of Allah is more rewardable, so he was okay with this, SubhanAllah. Another narration to show Sahabah's love for Hajj and the kind of importance they would give to Hajj: we learn about Abu Musa al-Ashari that a man asked him, 'O Abu Musa, I used to perform Hajj, that is, I used to perform when I was like younger or stronger, but now I'm weak and old, is there any action that is equal to Hajj? Like what else should I do? Like I cannot really do Hajj because I'm weak and old, what do I do?'

Abu Musa said: 'Do you have the power to free 70 believing slaves from the children of Ismail, and do you know of anything which is like going for Hajj, camping there and leaving from there?' And then he said, 'I can't find any action like it,' SubhanAllah. There's nothing like Hajj, we cannot say, 'Okay, if you can't do Hajj you do this,' SubhanAllah. This was the answer of Abu Musa al-Ashari Radiyallahu Anhu, and Allah knows best. And not only just Sahaba, but also our salaf as-salihin,

they also would give Hajj a lot of importance and they would perform a lot of Hajj as well. Let's look at this narration about Ta'us: Ta'us was asked, 'Nafl Hajj after the fard Hajj, is it better or charity is better? Like what should I do? Should I go for Hajj or give charity?' And SubhanAllah, such a valid question, because even today people ask this, isn't it? So, he responded: 'Where is the place to go and camp in Makkah? Where is the place to stay up late at night? Where is the place where you can go around the House of Allah?

Where is the place you can pray in it? Where is the place where you can stand on Arafat, gather and throw stones?' What does it mean by all of this? He was questioning him to make him think that there's nothing like that. Where else can you perform all of these acts of worship? Where else can you do tawaf? Where else can you find Arafat? Where else can you actually stone jamarat?

You can't, right? No matter where you try to do tawaf, it doesn't count; no matter which part of the earth you're going to go throw stones at someone or something, it's not going to be counted as worship, SubhanAllah. So, you cannot ignore or think that there is something else you can do instead of Hajj and it's still better. So, Hajj is a very heavy good deed, SubhanAllah. May Allah enable all of us to go there over and over again! So, about Ta'us—the same person who gave this answer, right, pay attention—about the same person, when he passed away, Ibn Shozab said: 'I attended the funeral of Ta'us in Makkah in 106 after Hijri.

I heard people saying, 'O Abdurrahman'—that's the name of Ta'us—'O Abdurrahman, may Allah have mercy on you, you have performed 40 Hajj,' SubhanAllah! The one who said this, he actually did it. So, this is however our salaf were: if he said there's nothing better than Hajj, he actually was performing a lot of Hajj, and that's what he believed in, and that's what he did, SubhanAllah. So, the words and actions, they match, and this is how we should be, Insha'Allah. May Allah make us among those who are truthful in their actions and also on their tongue!

And let's talk about some virtues, but before we get there, just wanted to share a few facts about how many Hajj people would perform back then. If Allah gives us the opportunity, we should also avail any opportunity, Insha'Allah, which comes our way. So, we learn that not only Ta'us performed 40 Hajj, but there were some Sahaba they performed more than 60 Hajj, and there were some Tabi'in and Taba Tabi'in, they performed more than 40 Hajj, SubhanAllah. And Ibn Masood

he was heard saying: 'There are two acts of worship in which I wish that everyone gets a share, like everyone gets to experience two things: and one was to travel for Hajj, second was to do Umrah,' SubhanAllah. This was his wish, that everyone should experience that and everyone should, Insha'Allah, have a share in it because it's very rewardable and it's very spiritual journey, and you change and you become better, SubhanAllah. Let's talk about the virtues of Hajj quickly.

So, best deed after iman is Hajj. If you look at the order, then it comes after jihad. So, let's look at this: Rasulullah was asked, 'Which is the best deed?' So, he responded: 'To believe in Allah and His Messenger.' He was then asked, 'Which is next?' Then he said, 'Jihad fi sabilillah.' Then he was asked, 'What is next?' So, he said, 'To perform Hajj Mabroor,' to perform a Hajj which is Mabroor. Insha'Allah we will talk about Mabroor in detail in one of the future sessions.

Another virtue of Hajj is that when we are on this way, when we are going, when we are traveling, when we are planning, then we are in the way of Allah. Indeed, Hajj and Umrah are from the way of Allah, and the people who go for Hajj and Umrah, they are called a delegation of Allah, SubhanAllah, such a beautiful title! 'The soldier in the cause of Allah and the pilgrim performing Hajj and Umrah are a delegation to Allah: He invited them, so they responded to Him, and they asked Him and He gives to them.'

He responds to their du'as as well, and du'as are granted, as we have just talked about, of hajjis and the ones who do Umrah. And sins are forgiven for the people who go for Umrah—and we have talked about this before as well, but this is a very beautiful narration, so we just want to touch base this part of it.
And verily the pilgrimage wipes out all the previous misdeeds, all the previous misdeeds, all evil deeds, all sins. And Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, He forgives the one who leaves the home for Hajj,

and it's a means to remove poverty and sin, we have talked about that before. And it's a jihad for the weak ones. Rasulullah said: 'Jihad of the elderly, the young, the weak, and woman is Hajj and Umrah,' SubhanAllah.

And SubhanAllah about this there was another narration where one person was asking Rasulullah and he was saying that, 'I'm very weak and, you know, I'm very coward, I cannot go for battle, I cannot go to defend Muslims, so what do I do?' So, Rasulullah told him: 'Jihad for the elderly, the young, the weak, and the woman is Hajj and Umrah,' SubhanAllah. So, we need to, Insha'Allah, go there to avail this amazing reward as well.

Aisha, she asked, 'Ya Rasulullah, shall we not go out for jihad with you?' He said, 'For you, the best and most beautiful type of jihad is Hajj'—and which Hajj? Al-Hajj al-Mabroor. So, Aisha, she said: 'So, I will not leave Hajj ever after hearing this from the Messenger of Allah Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam.' What does that mean? I will not miss the opportunity to perform Hajj. And May Allah also make us like her!
And we also learn that when we travel in the way of Allah, whatever trace whatever mark we experience—maybe a bruise, maybe a cut, whatever happens—it is also something which is of a lot of virtue.

So, let's look at this narration: 'A trace resulting in Allah's cause and a trace resulting from one of the duties that Allah made an obligation—they are more beloved to Allah than any other trace,' SubhanAllah, they are more beloved to Allah. You know, sometimes when you're performing duties, sometimes you do get some marks; for example, when you're sitting for salah, sometimes you get some marks on your feet because of, you know, sitting in the same position over and over again many times in a day.

Similarly at Hajj, if you get some cut, some bruise, that is also something which is very rewardable because Allah loves it. And a person who dies on the way to Hajj and Umrah—let's talk about them: whoever leaves for Hajj and dies, Allah writes for him the reward for Hajj till the Day of Judgment, SubhanAllah, as if he's keep on performing Hajj. And whoever leaves for Umrah and dies, Allah writes for him the reward for Umrah till the Day of Judgment. It should be Umrah here, and Allah knows best.

And the person who dies while performing Hajj, what will happen to that person on the Day of Judgment? Let's see: Narrated Ibn Abbas: 'While a man was riding in Arafat, he fell down from his ride and broke his neck and he passed away.'

Rasulullah Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam said: 'Wash him with water and sidr, and shroud him in two pieces of cloth, and neither perfume him nor cover his head, because he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection saying: Labbayka Allahumma Labbayk, like a pilgrim.' So, leave him like you're leaving him in the state of Ihram, don't cover his head, and he will be raised by saying Labbayk, SubhanAllah! Beautiful ending and beautiful beginning. And the people who perform Hajj, even if they do a lot of other bad deeds after that, eventually they will be taken out from Hell—that's another virtue of Hajj, SubhanAllah.

Let's say you're not able to go for Hajj this year or you really want to, but for whatever reason, you know, you feel really sad that you're not able to go for Hajj and you're missing out on a lot of reward. So, are there any deeds which are going to give you the same reward as Hajj? The answer is yes, Alhamdulillah. So, let's learn about them: when we perform Umrah in Ramadan, we are going to get the reward equal to Hajj.

There's another narration which talks about: Umrah during Ramadan is equal to Hajj in terms of rewards—but what kind of Hajj? Hajj with Rasulullah Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam. Another amazing opportunity we can all avail is praying our prayers in the masjid. So, do wudu, go to masjid and pray your prayers together in jamaah, right? It's for the brothers for sure, but for the sisters it's better for them to pray at home except in sacred masajid, right? Except in Haramain, except in Masjid al-Haram and Masjid an-Nabawi. So, Insha'Allah you can avail this opportunity when you go for Hajj and Umrah that you can go perform prayers there, but wherever you are and there is no fitna, you can go to masjid properly.

Another opportunity: praying Ishraq after Fajr. If you pray Fajr in jamaah, then sit remembering Allah at your prayer place until the sun rises, then you pray two rak'at, and you're going to get the reward like a complete Hajj and complete Umrah. Going to masjid to learn or to teach—that also gives us the reward of Hajj, SubhanAllah. So, what are we supposed to do? Go to the masjid not desiring anything except to learn deen or to teach deen.

What could be anything else? To meet up, to chitchat, to catch up—those should not be the reasons, or to promote your business, those are all wrong reasons, right? Reason to go to the masjid is to desire to learn or teach, and of course to pray and to please Allah, all of that. But based on this narration, to learn or to teach, a person is going to get the reward like Hajj. Jazakumullahu Khairan Katheera for paying attention. So, let's Insha'Allah conclude, right? that how can we be filthy in the House of Allah? How can we drop our used tissues, napkins there? How can we make it messy? How can we eat there and drop food particles there? Mina, Muzdalifah, Arafat—we should respect all Hajj sites, and we should respect all Hajj rituals and rites, and we should also respect all hujjaj there insha'Allah, because they all are there to worship Allah. Another aim and objective of Hajj is the sense of gratitude: that Alhamdulillah Allah called us, Alhamdulillah Allah gave me the opportunity that I can walk and do Hajj, or even if I'm not able to walk, I can sit and do Hajj on a wheelchair or on a cart.

So Alhamdulillah when people reach there, so this sense of gratitude develops automatically, but we also need to remind ourselves that we have to be more grateful that Allah called us here. All of them are standing in Arafat. So it's a good reminder for all of us that one day we will be standing in front of Allah on the Day of Judgment. And then let's just talk about Hajj rulings quickly, Insha'Allah. will build on them, so don't worry too much about the details, just jot down important points at this point. be the mandatory Hajj, right?
